title: Single-Engine Rate of Climb vs Density Altitude and Weight
conditions: Left engine inoperative, left propeller feathered, right engine full throttle, right propeller max RPM, mixture adjusted for smooth operation, gear and wing flaps retracted, optimum airspeed, cowl flaps open

verification.method: Sea-level ROC re-measured directly via column-cluster detection at the SL gridline. Each curve's own ceiling (ROC=0) point was located directly as the pixel where that curve first appears, working down from the top of the chart (the 3 curves do not cross; the lightest-weight curve simply extends highest before any of the others appear, since its ceiling is the highest of the three). Each 2-point line (SL + ceiling) was cross-checked against at least one independently measured mid-altitude point and matched within 1-3 ROC units.
verification.changeFromOriginal: daAtZero (service ceiling) values were already accurate in the original digitization (within 1-6.5%). seaLevel (SL rate of climb) was significantly underestimated for all three curves, worst for 3600 lb (150 -> 260 ft/min, a 73% relative error, though only 110 ft/min in absolute terms) and 3200 lb (300 -> 373, 24%); 2800 lb was closer (480 -> 520, 8%).
verification.confidence: High for all three curves — SL points directly measured at a clean, uncrowded part of the chart; ceiling points confirmed via two independent read methods (direct axis-intercept pixel read, and line-fit extrapolation from mid-altitude points) that agreed closely.
